chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The time for the Maghrib prayer during travel is until a quarter of the night.
ai.seo_question: What is the time limit for Maghrib prayer during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that during travel, the Maghrib prayer time extends until a quarter of the night has passed, reflecting the Shia principle of *taqdim* (earliness) combined with the concession of *ta'khir* (delay) for travelers. This ruling distinguishes the traveler's status from that of the resident, allowing for a more flexible window to pray Maghrib before Isha, thereby accommodating the fatigue and logistical challenges of journeying.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Aban Bin Usman, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The time for Al-Maghrib during the journey is up to a quarter of the night’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The time for al-Maghrib Salah (prayer) on a journey remains until passing of one-fourth of the night.’”
